purpose: Close the Gilbert-based land-air and patrol contribution that v039 omitted from the first FLINTLOCK-equivalent suppression calculation.

historical_anchor.Tarawa_specific: NHHC notes 44 Navy fighters, 7 Catalinas and 49 bombers at Tarawa, with B-24s staging there for Marshall strikes.

branch_adjustment.reason: Branch Gilbert capture is only days later than historical and FLINTLOCK-equivalent is also days later; by 2 Feb the construction clocks largely re-converge. GALVANIC fast-carrier losses do not erase Seabee/runway/base-force growth.

range_role_split.targets: Maloelap/Taroa, Wotje, Kwajalein/Roi depending load, weather and base
approach corridors, Japanese submarine lanes, base photography, rescue tracks

range_role_split.rule: Not projected to Roi/Taroa merely because physically present; northern distances and fuel reserve matter.

not_a_multiplier: Do not count patrol sorties as strike sorties.
Do not give Tarawa base-defense fighters a 580-nmi outbound northern-Marshall fighter sweep without a specific tank/range plan.
Land-air pressure can split Japanese attention and suppress outer bases, but TF58 still carries the decisive fighter-sweep/precision-airfield suppression against Taroa/Roi.
water_air_support: See MARSHALL_WATER_AVIATION_NETWORK_1944-02-02_WORKING_v001; PBY/PBM/tenders improve search, rescue, ASW and sustained patrol availability rather than becoming another bombing group.
